content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching the Sabbath is most commonly interpreted symbolically as God's rest — a type or foreshadowing of the spiritual rest believers find in Christ and, ultimately, of the eschatological rest of the people of God (salvation rest / heavenly rest). The weekly Sabbath, grounded in God's rest at creation, is read as pointing beyond itself to ceasing from one's own works and entering God's rest through faith in Christ.", "primary_basis": ["Genesis 2:2-3 (God rests on the seventh day and blesses it)", "Exodus 20:8-11 (Sabbath command grounded in creation rest)", "Deuteronomy 5:12-15 (Sabbath tied to redemption from Egypt)", "Hebrews 4:1-11 (a 'Sabbath rest remains for the people of God'; entering God's rest by faith)", "Matthew 11:28-30 (Christ's invitation, 'I will give you rest')", "Colossians 2:16-17 (Sabbaths as 'a shadow of things to come; the substance is Christ')", "Hebrews 3:7-19 (Israel's failure to enter rest as warning/type)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Christological fulfillment / shadow-typology: the Sabbath is a ceremonial shadow abolished or fulfilled in Christ, who is himself the believer's Sabbath; observance of the day is therefore no longer binding.", "basis": ["Colossians 2:16-17", "Romans 14:5-6", "Galatians 4:9-11", "Mark 2:27-28 ('the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath')"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Covenant-sign reading: the Sabbath as the distinguishing sign of God's covenant with Israel and of sanctification ('that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you').", "basis": ["Exodus 31:13-17", "Ezekiel 20:12, 20"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Transfer/creation-ordinance view (Reformed/Puritan sabbatarianism): the Sabbath is a perpetual moral command from creation, its symbolic and practical force transferred to the Lord's Day (Sunday) in honor of the resurrection.", "basis": ["Genesis 2:2-3", "Exodus 20:8-11", "Acts 20:7", "1 Corinthians 16:2", "Revelation 1:10"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Continuing seventh-day observance: the seventh-day Sabbath remains a binding command and an end-time sign of loyalty to God (Seventh-day Adventist and other sabbatarian traditions), often linked to the 'seal of God' in Revelation.", "basis": ["Exodus 20:8-11", "Isaiah 66:22-23", "Matthew 5:17-19", "Revelation 14:7, 12"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Millennial/cosmic-week typology (patristic): the seventh day prefigures a seventh 'millennial day' of world history or the world to come, as in the Epistle of Barnabas and some church fathers (also Augustine's 'eternal eighth day').", "basis": ["Genesis 2:2-3", "Psalm 90:4", "2 Peter 3:8", "Hebrews 4:9 (as read by patristic writers)"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Liberation/social-justice reading: the Sabbath as a symbol of release, humanitarian rest, and freedom from oppression and economic exploitation, tied to the exodus and jubilee patterns.", "basis": ["Deuteronomy 5:12-15", "Exodus 23:12", "Leviticus 25 (sabbatical year and jubilee)", "Isaiah 58:13-14", "Luke 4:16-21; Luke 13:10-16 (Sabbath healings as release)"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "There is broad, recognizable consensus across Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant interpretation that the Sabbath symbolizes rest in God, typologically fulfilled in Christ and consummated eschatologically (Hebrews 3-4 being the controlling text). Genuine disagreement lies not in the symbolism itself but in its practical entailments: whether a weekly observance continues (and on which day), which is where the Reformed sabbatarian, Lord's Day, and seventh-day traditions diverge. The covenant-sign, millennial-week, and liberation readings are usually treated as complementary layers rather than rivals to the 'rest in Christ' meaning."}
